plans.hypothesis: A two-segment, six-tendon structure with three tendons spanning the full robot and three acting only on the distal segment will provide independent proximal/distal bending authority sufficient to reach the off-axis target and settle within the frozen hold window.
plans.expected: The generated candidate is legal and exposes enough independent tendon routing authority for subsequent candidate-specific control optimization; optimized prediction or replay should approach the target without actuator-limit saturation and with terminal speed near zero.
plans.weakening: Generation is invalid, routing clearance fails, or candidate-specific optimization shows persistent large reach error or hold-speed violation despite converged control under the frozen bounds.
plans.interpretation: Success would support the structural-authority hypothesis only for this generated candidate; finite solver failure would be treated as inconclusive rather than structural infeasibility.

decision.selected_method: Generate a legal two-stage consecutive-span tendon layout, then perform candidate-specific control optimization and independent physical validation.

plans.hypothesis: A legal two-segment six-tendon design with three tendons spanning both segments and three confined to the distal segment can provide separable proximal and distal bending authority, allowing candidate-specific control optimization to reach the off-axis target and settle within every frozen terminal and hold constraint.
plans.expected: Generation returns a valid owned candidate with three full-length and three distal-only tendons arranged in opposing triads, suitable for subsequent candidate-specific control initialization and optimization.
plans.weakening: The routing remains invalid, or later converged candidate-specific optimization persistently misses reach or hold constraints without actuator saturation evidence attributable to finite solver failure.
plans.interpretation: A valid generation establishes only a legal unmeasured candidate. Task feasibility requires candidate-bound optimization and independent full-task physical evaluation.

decision.selected_method: Generate a clearance-conscious polar consecutive-span structure, then initialize and optimize candidate-specific control before independent physical evaluation.

plans.hypothesis: A legal two-segment six-tendon structure with three tendons spanning both segments and three tendons confined to the distal segment will provide separable proximal and distal bending authority, enabling candidate-specific control optimization to reach and hold the target.
plans.expected: Generation produces a valid owned candidate with two opposing three-tendon groups: one routed from segment 0 through segment 1 and one routed only over segment 1.
plans.weakening: The corrected routing is invalid, or later candidate-specific optimization and independent evaluation repeatedly fail reach or hold constraints under adequate bounded searches without evidence that the failures are merely finite-solver failures.
plans.interpretation: A valid candidate establishes only legal structure ownership, not task feasibility or acceptance. Reach/Hold feasibility must subsequently be established through candidate-specific control work and independent full-task physical evaluation.

plans.hypothesis: A legal two-segment, six-tendon structure within the frozen family can satisfy the full M3 reach-and-hold task when each proposed structure receives fresh Native control optimization; searching legal routing, lengths, sections, and materials without an inapplicable explicit span strategy will identify a feasible structure-control pair.
plans.expected: At least one generated legal structure completes candidate-specific Native control optimization and satisfies terminal error at or below 0.01 m, holding maximum error at or below 0.01 m, and holding maximum speed at or below 0.02 m/s over the frozen 0.5 s task.
plans.weakening: Across the bounded legal proposals, fresh Native control optimization either repeatedly fails numerically or independent full-task metrics remain above one or more frozen thresholds; finite search or solver failure will not be interpreted as structural infeasibility.
plans.interpretation: A passing independent Native evaluation supports feasibility of its exact structure-control pair only. Failures identify bounded-search outcomes and possible numerical or local-control limitations, not proof that the frozen family is infeasible.

plans.hypothesis: A fresh bounded legal structure-control co-design search that varies lengths, sections, materials, and routing while reoptimizing Native controls can find a candidate whose full-task Native trajectory meets all three frozen M3 Reach/Hold thresholds; the prior incomplete capability computations are treated only as solver failures, not structural infeasibility.
plans.expected: At least one legal proposal completes fresh candidate-specific Native control optimization and yields an executable full 0.5 s control sequence with terminal error no greater than 0.01 m, holding maximum error no greater than 0.01 m, and holding maximum speed no greater than 0.02 m/s; any apparent pass must then undergo independent physical replay.
plans.weakening: Across the bounded proposals, completed Native optimizations produce valid full-task trajectories but every trajectory exceeds at least one frozen threshold. Incomplete or numerically failed optimizations weaken only the solver route and will not be interpreted as structural infeasibility.
plans.interpretation: A completed candidate-specific Native trajectory meeting all modeled thresholds is a screening witness requiring independent physical replay, not formal acceptance. Completed valid misses compare structures at their measured scope; numerical failures diagnose optimization robustness only.

plans.hypothesis: A fresh legal bounded structure-control co-design search over segment lengths, material stiffness, section dimensions and tendon routing, with candidate-specific Native control reoptimization, can produce an executable full-horizon sequence that satisfies terminal position error, holding position error and holding speed limits simultaneously. The prior finite-budget Native observations motivate the variable choices but are not submitted as supporting evidence because they are not registered for empirical_search.
plans.expected: At least one newly constructed legal structure completes candidate-specific Native control optimization and has terminal position error at most 0.01 m, holding maximum position error at most 0.01 m and holding maximum speed at most 0.02 m/s over the frozen 0.5 s task, with a complete executable control sequence suitable for independent physical replay.
plans.weakening: Across the bounded proposals, completed Native optimizations yield valid complete trajectories but all exceed at least one frozen threshold. Numerical or optimization incompleteness weakens only this finite solver route and does not establish structural infeasibility.
plans.interpretation: A passing search result is a finite-budget Native co-design observation requiring exact independent full-task physical replay before acceptance. A failing or incomplete bounded search only characterizes this search route and budget.
